version.changelog: v2.6.0: 用户数据移到 ~/.web-access/（升级前请先备份 config.env 与 site-patterns，详见 references/migration-2.6.md）；任意 Chromium 内核浏览器可用（WEB_ACCESS_BROWSER 填用户数据目录，旧值 chrome/edge 兼容）；新增跨站 iframe 读取与坐标点击（/frames、/eval?frame=、/clickXY）；修复 proxy-maintenance restart 等问题。

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed browser-automation tool, but it grants long-running authenticated browser control and local browser-data access without enough containment.

dimensions.detail: A localhost CDP proxy bound to 127.0.0.1 can control the user's daily Chromium browser and logged-in pages; this is high-impact and not fully contained by authentication, Host, or Origin checks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is local scripts plus skill metadata requiring node and curl; no hidden package install or remote payload retrieval was found in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose many powerful operations, but broad natural-language triggers can lead to browser history/bookmark searches and session-backed browsing without clear per-use privacy consent or tight target scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The proxy is intentionally detached and long-running, stores configuration and site-pattern files under ~/.web-access, and has no idle service shutdown, which extends exposure beyond a single task.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Browser CDP automation fits the stated web-access purpose, but the skill also exposes arbitrary JavaScript evaluation, file-input injection, screenshots, authenticated-session use, anti-scraping bypass language, and local history/bookmark search for internal systems.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving a local helper broad control over your logged-in Chromium browser. Before use, understand that it can read page contents, act in authenticated sessions, inspect Chrome/Edge history and bookmarks when directed, attach local files to upload controls, and keep a localhost proxy running after a task ends. Prefer using it in a separate browser profile with limited accounts and stop the proxy when not needed.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: scripts/cdp-proxy.mjs exposes unauthenticated localhost endpoints for /targets, /eval, navigation, clicks, /setFiles, and /screenshot while connected to the user's authenticated browser.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: /screenshot writes to a caller-controlled path, /setFiles can attach local file paths to web forms, and find-url reads local browser data; these are powerful and under-scoped for routine web access.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md explicitly tells agents to search local bookmarks/history for prior pages and internal systems, which can expose sensitive browsing and organizational URLs from broad prompts.
[SSD-4] expected: Partly expected for the stated purpose of handling login-required and anti-scraping sites, but the skill normalizes authenticated browser reuse and bypass-oriented escalation with limited explicit consent gates.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: local browser history/bookmark access and persistent site-pattern writes are disclosed technically, but the user-facing privacy and retention controls are insufficient.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: the cited curl examples are primarily localhost proxy calls or user-directed target URLs, not evidence of hidden exfiltration by themselves.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the referenced browser-probe.mjs file is present and was inspected; it limits probing to application-data roots and does not itself read browser content.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-only instructions affect usability and locale expectations, but they are not a security concern supporting escalation.
